name: COVID-19 Mandatory Vaccination and Vaccination Program Policy Version 2
target: WA health system entities and employees in a Residential aged care facility
removal_method: 4/11/22 End of Public Health Emergency which removed all Public Health Directions made under the Emergency Declaration
removal_details:
Policy replaced by a newer version on 13/01/22 
06/19/21 Direction No.1 revoked by No.2 which added the "fully vaccinated by 17 November 2021" date
22/09/21 - Direction No.2 replaced by No.3 which added a "further public state of emergency made on 22/09/21" notice. No change in mandate requirements.  No revocation section
11/10/21 - No.3 revoked by No.4 which added a revocation section
compliance: First dose by 17 September 2021\nFully vaccinated by 17 November 2021
exemptions:
1. a permanent medical exemption authorised by a medical practitioner
2. a temporary medical exemption authorised by a medical practitioner
3. an authorised temporary exemption or exception due to the inability to access a
COVID-19 vaccine
4. an authorised temporary exemption or exception due to a critical workforce
shortage, to maintain the provision of quality of care or to protect the health and
safety of residents, or
5. an authorised exemption or exception related to another category in the relevant
state or territory public health order.
executive_orders: Residential Aged Care Facility Worker Access Directions.
enforcement_measures:
Unvaccinated Employees will initially be allowed to remain away from the workplace for a period
of two weeks without disciplinary action being commenced – the Preliminary Access Restriction
Period (PARP). The PARP provides time for the Employee to make a decision regarding their
intention to be Vaccinated and/or to receive a COVID-19 vaccine, prior to commencement of
formal disciplinary proceedings. The PARP will be unpaid.
Following the expiration of the two week PARP, the Employer may initiate disciplinary proceedings
in accordance with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Any decision to initiate disciplinary action, and subsequent disciplinary outcomes, will be
considered on a case by case basis and compliant with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Given the access restrictions provided for by the Aged Care Worker Directions, termination of
employment is a potential outcome for instances of non-compliance.
It is an offence for a person to fail, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any of these directions, punishable by a fine of up to $20,000 for individuals and $100,000 for bodies corporate.

name: Mandatory Vaccination Policy Phased Approach Group 1
target: Health care worker - Tier 3 health care facilities
removal_method: End of Public Health Emergency which removed all Public Health Directions made under the Emergency Declaration
removal_details:
13/01/2022 - policy replaced by a new version
16/09/21 - Direction No.1 revoked by No.2. No mandate changes
22/09/22 - No. 3 came into effect but directions doesn't have a revocation section, no mandate changes.
25/01/22 - No.3 revoked by No.4 which removed the exemption clause: "performing a law enforcement function that cannot reasonably be performed other than by entering the health care facility" and slightly altered a paragraph to "responding to an emergency where the emergency response is required to be provided immediately and a fully vaccinated or partially vaccinated person is not available to provide the response;"
compliance:
First dose by 01/12/21. Second dose by 01/01/22
evidence in the form approved by the Chief Health Officer that they have
been vaccinated against COVID-19, if:
(a) directed to do so by an emergency officer; or
(b) required to do so by their employer or by the owner, occupier or person
apparently in charge of a health care facility.
exemptions:
defined under the Directions
Medical exemption, or a Temporary exemption approved by the Chief Health Officer or their delegate, or as otherwise outlined in the Directions. Or if they are:
(a) performing a law enforcement function that cannot reasonably be performed
other than by entering the health care facility; or
(b) performing a statutory duty that cannot reasonably be performed other than by entering the health care
facility; or
(c) performing any function or duty or exercising any right or power under a Fair
Work entry permit; or
(d) responding to an emergency in a capacity other than as a health care worker or
a health support worker; or
(e) providing emergency care to a patient in the health care facility where the
emergency care is necessary to be provided immediately and a fully vaccinated
or a partially vaccinated health care worker or health support worker is not available to provide that emergency care
Or an ad hoc volunteer
enforcement_measures:
Unvaccinated Employees will initially be allowed to remain away from the workplace for a period
of two weeks without disciplinary action being commenced – the Preliminary Access Restriction
Period (PARP). The PARP provides time for the Employee to make a decision regarding their
intention to be Vaccinated and/or to receive a COVID-19 vaccine, prior to commencement of
formal disciplinary proceedings. The PARP will be unpaid.
Following the expiration of the two week PARP, the Employer may initiate disciplinary proceedings
in accordance with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Any decision to initiate disciplinary action, and subsequent disciplinary outcomes, will be considered on a case by case basis and compliant with the Discipline Policy and Procedures.
Given the access restrictions provided for by the Aged Care Worker Directions, termination of
employment is a potential outcome for instances of non-compliance.
It is an offence for a person to fail, without reasonable excuse, to comply with any of these
directions, punishable by a fine of up to $20,000 for individuals and $100,000 for bodies
corporate.

notes:
What counts as a “critical business site”, i.e. where "critical business workers" work:

1) Critical accommodation premises 
- Hotels, motels or other accommodation facilities (to the extent they provide accommodation).

- Caravan parks and camping grounds (excluding residential parks). 

2) Critical hospitality premises 

- Restaurants, cafés, pubs, bars or clubs (not nightclubs), including food courts, shopping-centre outlets and food trucks/vehicles; dine-in, takeaway or delivery.

- Truckstops/roadhouses.

- Distilleries, breweries and wineries only to the extent they provide food for on-site consumption, takeaway or delivery. 

3) Critical retail, service or distribution premises 

- Supermarket, grocery store, butcher, fruit & veg store, fishmonger.

- Retail bakery; bulk food shop; health-food shop.

- Permanent indoor/outdoor markets to the extent they sell groceries/meat/fruit/veg/fish/fresh or prepared food.

- Bank/credit union/building society shopfront.

- Retail hardware store.

- Food distribution centres (excluding manufacturers).

- Petrol stations (including those that sell groceries/food).

- Veterinary clinics/hospitals.

- Funeral, burial, cremation premises (including funeral parlours, crematoria). 

4) Plus: any other premises or class of premises specified in writing by the Chief Health Officer under the Directions.
